original_sender_chain.observation: First full update writes SERVER_ALLENTS, increments lastSentFullUpdateID and marks the packet ordered while that ID is unacknowledged. This ordering does not require a prior client application acknowledgment.

Compression occurs before sibling splitting. Default payload split is sendPacketBufferSize minus housekeeping allowance. A child is created per part, assigned the common sibling group/count and its part index, made compatible, and enqueued with sibling_packet=(part!=0).
PacketMemoryPool uses default zeroed allocation; only the separate bitstream buffer pool disables zeroing. pktMakeCompatible copies reliable/debug/compress/ordered flags, not ordered_id.
Initialization selects Default; allocation zeroes the entire record when zeroMemory is enabled. MemoryPool.h defines Default=ZERO_MEMORY_BIT.
Every queued child receives its own packet ID. Only an ordered UDP first child (!sibling_packet) receives a new ordered_id. The later zero-initialized children retain ordered_id=0.

The wrapper serializes sibling count and part as BitsPack(1), group as 32 bits, and ordered flag plus BitsAuto(ordered_id) for every ordered child. Zero is encodable/readable. Siblings are sorted by part; merged ID, flags and ordered_id are taken from part0.
